titulo: Rare sugar d-sorbose may help control allergic and autoimmune diseases
resumo: Rare sugars are naturally occurring monosaccharides that are scarce in nature and are not readily used by the body as energy sources. Some have physiological effects beyond sweetness, raising interest in their potential health applications. One such sugar, d-sorbose, is a structural relative of d-fructose, but its effects on immune cells have remained unclear. Regulatory T cells (Tregs), identified by the Foxp3 protein, help restrain excessive immune responses and maintain immune balance. Whether a rare sugar can promote these cells has been little explored.
